grants.sshTunnel: BigQuery does not run through an SSH tunnel: every request goes over HTTPS to Google's API hosts, and a tunnel forwards one address of the several the provider reaches. Turn the tunnel off.

reasons.agentCredentialForm: A service-account key JSON, from which the provider mints its own token at the scope it asks for.

grants.sshTunnel: Apache Cassandra does not run through an SSH tunnel: the tunnel forwards one address, and the driver reaches every other node of the ring at the address that node advertises. Connect to the cluster directly, or turn the tunnel off.

reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_read_query runs under the boundary agent mode uses, a role proven before every statement to hold only SELECT on the connection's keyspace, on a server that enforces it, and a provider check that sends one SELECT of that keyspace or of system_schema (docs/providers/cassandra.md section 14).
Opened on its own: run_read_query runs under the boundary agent mode uses, `readonly = 1` on every request and a user proven at open to hold only reads (docs/providers/clickhouse.md section 5.6).

grants.sshTunnel: Couchbase does not run through an SSH tunnel: the tunnel forwards one port, and queries go to the query service, on another port, at the address the cluster's node map advertises. Turn the tunnel off.

reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_read_query runs under the boundary agent mode uses, a user whose only roles are query_select on named scopes of the bucket, checked at open and again before every statement on a server proven to enforce it, and a fence that sends one SELECT (docs/providers/couchbase.md section 15).

reasons.writeReach: No read-only mode: the provider sends the statement the editor holds, as Db2's does.
reasons.metadataReadChangesState: A Databend Cloud call resumes a suspended warehouse, which bills while it runs; the row is per engine, so a self-hosted server, which never bills, is marked too.

reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_read_query runs under the boundary agent mode uses, a user checked before every statement, on the statement's own connection, to hold nothing but CONNECT and SELECT (docs/providers/db2.md section 10.1).

reasons.writeReach: Druid native SQL refuses a write, but that is the engine's grammar: Studio sends the statement the editor holds.
reasons.statementRead: Agent mode executes statements on Druid, and MCP read stays closed on it until a change of its own opens it: a LOOKUP of a literal key is kept out by the statement fence alone (backlog B151).

grants.sshTunnel: DuckDB opens a file on the Studio server, so there is no address for an SSH tunnel to forward to. Turn the tunnel off: edit the connection and save it again.
grants.servesOneSession: It keeps one read-write handle per database file, as SINGLE_WRITER_FILE records, so a second session would be a second handle on the file.

reasons.readsFileAccessPosture: The engine whose editor handle opens under the posture: external access off for every role but admin, and for every role on a seed a non-admin role can use. SQLite refuses a denied handle instead.
reasons.deniedFileAccessRefusal: It reads the posture too, and confines a denied handle instead of refusing it.
reasons.opensLocalFile: A database file (or `:memory:`) opened by the native DuckDB addon in Studio's own process.

reasons.writeReach: As Druid: the SQL grammar has no write, and Studio sends whatever the editor holds.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_read_query runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the SQL endpoint's grammar, which holds no write, on a server checked at open to be the release line whose write refusals were captured (docs/providers/elasticsearch.md section 5.9). OpenSearch, served by the same provider directory, has a row of its own.
reasons.agentCredential: The transport sends the API key pair in preference to user and password (src/lib/db/providers/sql/search/http-transport.ts), so an agent pair beside it would run under the key.

reasons.writeReach: The first engine that keeps the mode (#1089 E6): its provider refuses every write command, value edit and maintenance operation before any request while the mode holds (`write-policy.ts`).
reasons.exposable: Offered with every answer metadata only, as agent mode reads it: key names and values carry secrets, so `inspect_schema` lists no key prefix, since every agent-mode handle withholds them, and `run_etcd_read` answers the closed table's names, counts and sizes under a user the server proves reads only, on no Kubernetes storage prefix and not on every key.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_etcd_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the provider's closed table of metadata reads and a user the server shows, before every command, to hold no root role and only READ, on no Kubernetes storage prefix and not on every key, with every answer projected to names, counts and sizes (docs/providers/etcd.md section 15.7).

grants.sshTunnel: Firestore does not run through an SSH tunnel: every request goes over TLS to Google's API hosts, and a tunnel forwards one address of the several the provider reaches. Turn the tunnel off.

reasons.writeReach: Read-only whatever the flag says: the client builds only the read requests of its closed table, before any socket, and the provider offers no object edit and no maintenance operation.
reasons.exposable: Closed: every read is billed to the user's project, an MCP call has an allowance of its own and nothing bounds billed reads across calls, `inspect_schema` carries no allowance, so no collection listing reaches it, and a production viewer role is not measured (backlog B107).
reasons.statementRead: Agent mode executes metadata-only reads on Firestore, and MCP read stays closed on it: every read is billed and nothing bounds billed reads across MCP calls (backlog B107).

reasons.writeReach: Read-only whatever the flag says: on 1.x and 2.x the InfluxQL lexer policy (`src/lib/languages/influxql/policy.ts`) is the only boundary between a Studio user and `DROP DATABASE`, so it refuses every statement that is not one `SELECT`, `SHOW` or `EXPLAIN` before any request; the route table reaches no write endpoint.
reasons.exposable: Both offered for the metadata tools, which list database, measurement and column names and types only. Both providers implement `queryReadOnly` for agent mode; `run_read_query` serves InfluxDB 3's SQL, opened by MCP_STATEMENT_READ, and no MCP statement tool reads InfluxQL, so `influxdb` stays closed there (backlog B94).
reasons.statementRead: Agent mode executes InfluxQL on InfluxDB, and MCP read stays closed on it: on 1.x a catalog SHOW's database scope rests on the agent's statement reader alone, and no layer that reads the answer can hold it (backlog B94).

reasons.writeReach: Read-only whatever the flag says: the closed route table reaches no write, configure, token, cache or plugin endpoint, the SQL policy refuses every statement that does not lead with a read keyword before any request, and the 3.12 planner refuses every write besides.
reasons.agentCredentialForm: The agent's token, sent as the bearer credential instead of the connection's own.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_read_query runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the 3.12 Core planner's write refusals on a server checked at open to be that line, behind the read policy and the system schema fence (docs/providers/influxdb3.md section 3.5).

grants.sshTunnel: Kafka does not run through an SSH tunnel: the tunnel forwards one address, and a Kafka client reads from every broker the cluster advertises, at the address the broker advertises. Connect to the brokers directly.

reasons.writeReach: Read-only whatever the flag says: the client sends only the read APIs of `KAFKA_READ_APIS`, and a live run left the topic list, every end offset and every group's committed offsets unchanged after every provider surface.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_kafka_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, a client that holds the Metadata and ListOffsets reads alone, answered metadata-only with a platform's own topics withheld (docs/providers/kafka.md section 16).

reasons.writeReach: Read-only whatever the flag says: the request policy admits GET and the three self reviews only, before any socket, and the provider offers no object edit and no maintenance operation.
reasons.agentCredentialForm: The agent's bearer token, whose RBAC bounds what the agent reads.
reasons.exposable: Offered with every answer machine-redacted: `run_kubectl_read` runs the agent's `queryReadOnly`, whose output masks every Secret name, and `inspect_schema` lists relations alone, which no Kubernetes kind is, so no object name, a Secret's included, reaches it.

grants.sshTunnel: LibreDB opens a file on the Studio server, so there is no address for an SSH tunnel to forward to. Turn the tunnel off: edit the connection and save it again.
grants.servesOneSession: It keeps one read-write handle per database file, as SINGLE_WRITER_FILE records, so a second session would be a second handle on the file.

reasons.writeReach: Studio's own store: the editor sends `put` and `delete`, and no gate refuses them on a connection.
reasons.agentCredentialForm: An embedded store has no principal to sign an agent in as.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_libredb_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, a read-only handle of its own for every command, opened through Studio's read-only file adapter, which takes no lock and cannot write; the seed names the one file it reads, Studio's own storage and credential files are refused as a target, and the file's reserved internal namespace is left out of every answer (docs/providers/libredb.md section 15).
reasons.metadataReadChangesState: The operations open holds the file's exclusive lock until the handle has been idle for 30 minutes.
reasons.opensLocalFile: The embedded store this app creates, a file on Studio's own volume.

reasons.agentCredentialForm: The agent's bearer token for the database, sent instead of the connection's own.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_read_query runs under the boundary agent mode uses, a token proven at open to be read-only and refused every write by the server (docs/providers/libsql.md section 3.6).

reasons.writeReach: Its provider refuses Load and Release before any request while the mode holds, and every v1 console request is a read (vector-family E8).
reasons.exposable: Offered for the metadata tools (vector-family E17), and for `run_milvus_read`, which MCP_STATEMENT_READ opens on it.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_milvus_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the provider's closed RPC table and a user the server proves read-only before every request, every call naming a collection sent only when the user's own collection list holds it, every answer projected to names, counts and flags (docs/providers/milvus.md, section Agent mode).

maskingExemptColumns.reason: The PDU register number this row answered for, not a postal address, so it is shown as it was read.

grants.servesOneSession: Its tree is the connection's register map, so a second session would only dial a device that may serve one client at a time.

reasons.writeReach: Structural rather than configured: the encoder names four read function codes and device identification, and there is no code in the provider that can build a write (#1723 MB-S1, `src/lib/db/providers/industrial/modbus/valve.ts` re-checks every outbound byte).
reasons.exposable: Closed: agent mode reads the device paced per device and counted per run, and MCP has no run, so nothing would bound a client's device requests across calls; a cancelled call keeps the device's lane until its read's own deadline; and no MCP surface lists the register map's points, so a client could form only a block read whose decoding it guesses (backlog B160).
reasons.statementRead: Agent mode executes paced reads on Modbus, and MCP read stays closed on it: no bound on device requests across calls, no lane release on cancel and no register-map surface exist for MCP yet (backlog B160).

grants.servesOneSession: Its tree reads nothing from the broker, so a second session would only cost one more broker read at its open.

reasons.writeReach: Structural rather than a mode: the encoder has no function that writes a PUBLISH, so there is no write to enforce against. The valve repeats the check on the bytes.
reasons.exposable: Offered with every answer metadata only, as agent mode reads it: topic names and payloads are withheld, so `inspect_schema` refuses an MQTT connection by name, since a broker declares no relation kind, and `run_mqtt_read` answers one window's totals or one named topic's counts and flags, with its window and the completeness sentence.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_mqtt_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the provider's closed five-packet encoder and valve, which send no PUBLISH and no Will, with every answer projected to one window's counts and flags, never a topic name or a payload, and carrying its window and the completeness sentence as notes (docs/providers/mqtt.md section 15).

reasons.writeReach: Structural rather than a mode: the request table holds nine routes and every one of them is a GET, so there is no write to enforce against (`src/lib/db/providers/industrial/mtconnect/routes.ts`).
reasons.exposable: Offered for the metadata tools and run_mtconnect_read, which acquire an agent-mode handle and so read the device model with the agent's adapter connections withheld.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_mtconnect_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the provider's closed table of nine GET routes, with the agent's adapter connections withheld from every answer (docs/providers/mtconnect.md section 14).

reasons.writeReach: Read-only whatever the flag says: this version of the provider refuses every write before it is sent, offers no object edit and no maintenance operation, so a connection marked read-only keeps the promise.
reasons.exposable: Offered for the metadata tools, `list_connections` and `inspect_schema` (Neo4j spec 6.4), and for `run_cypher_read`, which MCP_STATEMENT_READ opens on it.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_cypher_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, on Enterprise Edition only, a user the server proves before every statement to hold only reads, no LOAD and no extension it can execute, and the server's own classification of every statement (docs/providers/neo4j.md section 15).

grants.servesOneSession: It holds one NETCONF session per provider, and a device may admit few sessions, none measured, so a second session could be refused where the editor's answers.

reasons.writeReach: Structural rather than a mode: the request builder writes four read bodies and `<close-session>`, and no function in the provider builds an `<edit-config>` or any other write (`src/lib/db/providers/network/netconf/requests.ts`).
reasons.exposable: Closed: agent mode reads NETCONF configuration and state with keys, password hashes, access rules and every node the device's own YANG marks nacm:default-deny-all withheld by Studio alone, since a read-only account still reads password hashes and keystore entries (docs/providers/netconf.md 6.3), and nothing on the device is proved to hold them out; the rest is the device's whole configuration (backlog B159).
reasons.statementRead: Agent mode executes reads on NETCONF with the withheld nodes pruned, and MCP read stays closed on it: the pruning is Studio's alone, with no device layer proved to hold the secrets out (backlog B159).

grants.servesOneSession: Its tree lists no node, so a second session would only take one more of the server's sessions at its open.

reasons.writeReach: Structural rather than a mode: the client seam names eight read services and none of them writes, so there is no write to enforce against (`src/lib/db/providers/industrial/opcua/client.ts`).
reasons.exposable: Offered only beneath the read roots its seed declares, which READ_ROOTS_REQUIRED holds MCP to: an OPC UA server declares no relation kind, so `inspect_schema` refuses an OPC UA connection by name, and `run_opcua_read` answers every node outside the roots exactly as a missing one.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_opcua_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the provider's read-only client over a session opened per read, reading only beneath the seed's read roots, proved by a walk down from them on that session, with every other node id answered as a missing one and nothing sent for it (docs/providers/opcua.md section 15).
reasons.hostPathFields: The client certificate and private key a seed connection names, read by the OPC UA library from the host.

reasons.writeReach: As Elasticsearch, and the server's own DELETE can be switched on in 2.x.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_read_query runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the SQL plugin's refusal of every write, on a server whose DELETE is proved off and whose release line was checked at open, with a statement check that keeps hidden and dot-led indices from each statement (docs/providers/opensearch.md section 5.9).

Opened on its own: run_read_query runs under the boundary agent mode uses, a user set READ ONLY, checked before every statement on that statement's own session to reach nothing READ ONLY leaves open and to hold no grant on a schema Oracle maintains beyond the policy catalogs (docs/providers/oracle.md section 5.7).

reasons.writeReach: Read-only whatever the flag says: the adapter's stub holds only `GetShardAssignments`, `Read`, `List`, `RangeScan` and `Health/Check` (O8), and the parser refuses every write verb by name, naming the read-only mode while it holds (O1).
reasons.exposable: Closed: the 0.18.0 server authorizes nothing, so a token reads, writes and deletes every key of every namespace and the provider's closed table would be the only layer between an MCP client and the cluster; Oxia key paths name Pulsar tenants, namespaces and topics, and no MCP surface that lists no key name is designed (backlog B100).
reasons.statementRead: Agent mode executes metadata-only reads on Oxia, and MCP read stays closed on it: the server authorizes nothing, so the closed table would be the only layer between an MCP client and every key (backlog B100).

reasons.serverLevelWithoutDatabase: An empty `database` on discrete fields reaches the whole server (`serverLevel` in providers/sql/postgres.ts); a connection string never does.

reasons.writeReach: Read-only whatever the flag says: the transport requests only the closed endpoint table `PATHS`, every one a read, and a live run left the TSDB's series count unchanged after every provider surface.
reasons.statementRead: Closed: Prometheus has no principal that narrows a read, so the connection's credential reaches every series the TSDB stores, and no layer independent of reading the expression narrows it; agent mode reads under that reach with the flags and every URL's userinfo and query string withheld (backlog B161).

reasons.writeReach: Every v1 console request is a read and the provider has no maintenance operation, and while the mode holds it refuses every route that is not a read before any request (vector-family spec 4.4).
reasons.agentCredentialForm: The agent's API key or JWT, sent instead of the connection's own.
reasons.exposable: Offered for the metadata tools, carrying names and types only (vector-family spec 4.4), and for `run_qdrant_read`, which MCP_STATEMENT_READ opens on it.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_qdrant_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the provider's closed table of read routes and a key the server refuses an empty alias update and an empty point delete on every collection it lists, before every request, with every answer projected to names, counts and flags (docs/providers/qdrant.md, section Agent mode).

grants.sshTunnel: RabbitMQ connections cannot use an SSH tunnel: one tunnel carries one port, and the management API and AMQP use two.

reasons.writeReach: Read-only whatever the flag says: the management client's closed route table holds GET routes only, and the AMQP client has no encoder for a publish, a get, a reject or any queue or exchange method, so no request path writes.
reasons.exposable: Offered for the metadata tools, carrying stream names and the fixed read columns only, and for `run_rabbitmq_read`, which reads through agent mode's metadata-only path: each message's offset and body size, never a message value (backlog B108).
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_rabbitmq_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the provider's structural closed table (a read client that encodes no take, publish, purge or declare, the stream-only type check before any frame and the `x-stream-offset` 406 backstop), answered metadata only, each message's offset and body size; message values stay withheld (docs/providers/rabbitmq.md section 17, backlog B108).

Opened on its own: run_redis_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the closed table of metadata reads and an ACL user the server refuses every write probe before every command, on that command's own connection, with every answer projected to counts, types and sizes (docs/providers/redis.md section 16).

reasons.writeReach: Read-only whatever the flag says: the console's closed command table reaches no write, and the provider sends only GET and HEAD.
reasons.agentCredentialForm: An access key ID and secret of its own: an agent key ID equal to the connection's names the same key.
reasons.exposable: Offered with every answer metadata only, as agent mode reads it, and only under the seed's agent read key, which MCP_AGENT_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED requires: object keys are withheld, so `inspect_schema` refuses an S3 connection by name, since a bucket declares no relation kind, and `run_s3_read` answers bucket names, counts and flags under that key's grants.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_s3_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the provider's closed table of six metadata reads over a transport that sends GET and HEAD only, with every answer projected to names, counts and flags, never an object key or value, signed with the seed's agent read key alone, whose grants hold the bucket scope (docs/providers/s3.md section 15.7).
reasons.agentCredentialRequired: The agent read key's grants are the only layer that holds the buckets an MCP client reaches: the connection's own key may read every bucket, and S3 has no read-only principal Studio can prove.
reasons.agentCredential: An access key ID and secret of its own: an agent key ID equal to the connection's names the same key.

grants.sshTunnel: SNMP does not run through an SSH tunnel: the tunnel forwards TCP, and SNMP reads travel as UDP datagrams. Turn the tunnel off.
grants.servesOneSession: Its tree is the bundled catalog, so a second session would only probe the agent once more at its open.

reasons.writeReach: Structural rather than a mode: the statement grammar holds four read commands (get, next, walk, table), and the valve refuses a Set PDU on every datagram it can read (`src/lib/db/providers/network/snmp/valve.ts`).
reasons.exposable: Offered as agent mode reads it: values are the device's own readings, and the withheld subtrees (the security and target modules, the running processes, the commands the agent runs and the vendor copy tables) are decided on every answer, so `inspect_schema` lists the bundled catalog's tables and scalar groups, none inside a withheld subtree, and `run_snmp_read` steps over or answers withheld every one a read reaches.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_snmp_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the agent's client of Get, GetNext and GetBulk alone behind the valve, with every withheld subtree decided by the prefix of every identifier an answer carries, and its reasons carried as notes; a v2c community is no principal, so the agent's own view and Studio's withheld set are the data scope (docs/providers/snmp.md section 14).

grants.sshTunnel: Snowflake does not run through an SSH tunnel: the driver reaches the account's Snowflake hosts over HTTPS, and a tunnel forwards one address. Turn the tunnel off.

grants.servesOneSession: Its tree is the session's own connect read, so a second session would answer another read's snapshot after a broker read of its own.

reasons.writeReach: Structural rather than a mode, and the structure is an absence: `encoder.ts` encodes CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, PINGREQ and DISCONNECT and has no function that writes a PUBLISH, while the CONNECT takes no will parameter at all, so no later edit can register a death certificate by passing a value (5.4).
reasons.exposable: Offered with every answer metadata only, as agent mode reads it: ids, metric names and values are withheld, so `inspect_schema` answers an empty page, since an agent-mode handle declares no kind, and `run_sparkplug_read` answers one window's totals or one named object's counts, with its window and the completeness sentence.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_sparkplug_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the provider's closed encoder, which sends no PUBLISH, command or Will, with every answer projected to one window's counts and flags, never an id, a metric name or a value, and carrying its window and the completeness sentence as notes (docs/providers/sparkplug.md section 15).

grants.deniedFileAccessRefusal: SQLite connections require an administrator because this driver cannot confine statement-level file access
grants.sshTunnel: SQLite opens a file on the Studio server, so there is no address for an SSH tunnel to forward to. Turn the tunnel off: edit the connection and save it again.

reasons.deniedFileAccessRefusal: Its open refuses a denied handle before it opens anything, and the provider factory before it is built.
reasons.opensLocalFile: A database file opened through `bun:sqlite` or `node:sqlite` in Studio's own process.
reasons.servesOneSession: A file serves a second session; an in-memory database is another database per handle, which the class reads from the connection.

reasons.statementRead: Agent mode executes statements on Trino, and MCP read stays closed on it: the read-only access control lets every identity read other users' query text in `system.runtime.queries`, and only the statement fence keeps it out (backlog B166).

reasons.writeReach: As Qdrant (#1566 spec 3.5): every console request is a read, the provider has no maintenance operation, and it refuses every route that is not a read, and every request that would wake a cold tenant, before any request.
reasons.agentCredentialForm: The agent's API key, sent instead of the connection's own.
reasons.exposable: As Milvus and Qdrant (#1566 spec 3.5): offered for the metadata tools, and for `run_weaviate_read`, which reads one metadata request under the agent's own boundary; inspect_schema lists a collection's properties and vectors and never its tenants or aliases.
reasons.statementRead: Opened on its own: run_weaviate_read runs under the boundary agent mode uses, the provider's closed table of read requests and a key the server proves before every read to hold the viewer role's read actions only, answered through the metadata-only projection (docs/providers/weaviate.md section 15).
